samples.summary: Image-resize commit writes to the document with no `readOnly` check of its own; the change moved the only read-only gate from the top of `handleImageMouseDown` into one branch
samples.evidence: Before this change `handleImageMouseDown` began with `if (readOnly) return;`. The diff deletes that and re-gates only the handle branch (`if (!readOnly && selectedImage)`, editor.ts:2559). The mutation itself — `handleImageResizeMouseUp` → `docStore.snapshot(); doc.applyInlineStyle({...}, { image: merged })` (editor.ts:2512-2520) — carries no `readOnly` check, and neither does `handleImageResizeMouseMove`. I traced every assignment to `imageResizeDrag` (grep `imageResizeDrag = ` → editor.ts:2497, 2567, 3856) and found no second entry point, so there is no live bypass today: the single branch condition is the whole enforcement. That makes it a one-line-deep gate protecting a CRDT write, and the branch's own task note concedes it is unpinned (`docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md`, "Known coverage gap": "That gate is the only thing stopping a viewer from resizing — the resize commit carries no readOnly check of its own... removing it would not turn any test red"). Impact if it regresses is a real unauthorized write, not merely cosmetic: the server-side Yorkie auth webhook that would otherwise deny a viewer's `rw` push runs in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105, which returns allow on every deny while unenforced), so for an anonymous `role: 'viewer'` share link the client-side `readOnly` flag is currently the effective write boundary. Suggest an `if (readOnly) return;` at the top of `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (and/or in the commit helper) so the write site is self-guarding rather than trusting one caller.

samples.summary: `imageKeyHandler` is dispatched ahead of `handleKeyDown`'s read-only guard, and this change makes that handler reachable in read-only for the first time
samples.evidence: `handleKeyDown` consults `this.imageKeyHandler(e)` at text-editor.ts:865 and only reaches the `if (this.readOnly)` guard at text-editor.ts:894. Until this change `selectedImage` could never be non-null in a read-only mount in production (`handleImageMouseDown` returned early on `readOnly`, and grep shows no frontend caller of `selectImageAt` — `grep -r 'selectImageAt|getSelectedImage|clearImageSelection' packages/frontend/src` returns nothing), so the handler always returned false immediately and the ordering was inert. The diff enables read-only click-selection, so every branch inside the handler now executes in a document the user may not write. I checked each branch: Escape and the arrow branches only touch `cursor`/`selection` (view state); Cmd/Ctrl+C and Cmd/Ctrl+X return true and defer to the native clipboard events, where `handleCut` self-guards (text-editor.ts:1237); Delete/Backspace reach `deleteSelectedImageInline`, which self-guards (editor.ts:2283). So there is no mutating branch unguarded *today*. The defect is structural: the read-only decision now lives in per-branch checks inside a handler that deliberately runs before the enforced guard, so any branch added later is write-enabled by default in read-only — and with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the client gate is what actually stops an anonymous viewer share from writing. Worth an explicit `if (readOnly)` early-return for the mutating subset (or moving the handler call below the read-only guard for keys that can mutate).

samples.summary: `handleImageHover` is not read-only gated, so a viewer gets resize cursors over handles the overlay does not draw and the editor refuses — contradicting the branch's own claim that the hover cursor stays gated
samples.evidence: `handleImageHover` (editor.ts:2737-2750) hit-tests `hitTestImageHandle(selRect, x, y)` and sets `canvas.style.cursor = cursorForHandle(handle)` with no `readOnly` check, and it is installed unconditionally at editor.ts:2751-2753. Now that a read-only viewer can select an image (`handleImageMouseDown`'s top-level `if (readOnly) return;` removed), hovering the handle hotspots of the selected image shows nwse/ns/ew resize cursors even though `drawImageSelection(..., { handles: false })` (doc-canvas.ts:683) paints no handles and the drag branch declines. That advertises a write affordance the permission model refuses. It also makes the task note false where it states "the resize-handle branch and the hover cursor stay gated" (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md, fourth-review-round bullet) — a security-posture claim in the docs that the code does not implement.

samples.summary: Image mousedown in read-only now stops propagation before `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` can refresh `readOnlyPendingLinkHref`, so a stale link can be opened by the following mouseup
samples.evidence: In read-only, `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` records the link under the pointer (`this.readOnlyPendingLinkHref = this.getLinkHrefAtMouse(e) ?? null`, text-editor.ts:1667-1669) and `handleMouseUp` opens it on a collapsed click (text-editor.ts:1991-2002). Previously `handleImageMouseDown` returned at the top on `readOnly`, so every read-only mousedown reached that assignment and reset the pending href. After this change an image-body hit calls `e.stopImmediatePropagation()` (editor.ts:2590), so the assignment is skipped while the subsequent container `mouseup` still runs. If a pending href survived an earlier interaction (mousedown on a link, pointer dragged outside the container, button released there, so no `handleMouseUp` consumed it), the next click on an image opens that stale URL in a new tab — and `selectImageInline` sets `selection.setRange(null)`, guaranteeing the `collapsed` condition passes. The href is still filtered by `isSafeUrl`, so this is unexpected navigation rather than script execution. Clearing/refreshing `readOnlyPendingLinkHref` on the image-hit path would close it.

samples.summary: The new `imageDeleteHandler` / `imageSelectionProvider` hooks are installed on `TextEditor` unconditionally, bypassing the read-only API allowlist; safe today only because of two independent inner guards
samples.evidence: editor.ts:3903-3919 neutralizes mutating EditorAPI methods in read-only via a hand-maintained allowlist (`MUTATING_METHODS`), described in-comment as the guard for "the programmatic EditorAPI ... reachable by any holder of `api`". The new document-mutating capability handed to `TextEditor` — `textEditor.imageDeleteHandler = deleteSelectedImageInline` (editor.ts:2319) — is wired regardless of `readOnly` and is not covered by that boundary. It is currently safe twice over: `handleCut` returns before invoking it in read-only (text-editor.ts:1237-1240), and `deleteSelectedImageInline` itself starts with `if (readOnly || !selectedImage) return;` (editor.ts:2283). Flagging only because the allowlist comment claims the API boundary is the catch-all for programmatic mutation and this capability now sits outside it; no bypass traced.

verdict.reason: The commit site genuinely has no readOnly line of its own, but the write is unreachable for a read-only viewer, so there is no authorization gap to block on. `imageResizeDrag` is assigned only at editor.ts:2567 and the document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners are attached only at editor.ts:2578-2579, both nested inside `if (!readOnly && selectedImage)` (editor.ts:2559); every other reference is a read or a `= null` teardown (editor.ts:2497, 3856), and both resize handlers early-return on null drag state (editor.ts:2464, 2489). In read-only the handlers are never even attached. The programmatic surface is independently gated: the read-only API neutralizer no-ops every mutating EditorAPI method incl. updateSelectedImage/insertImage (editor.ts:3903-3921). The repo also documents that this flag is a client-side convenience and the store/server is the authoritative boundary (editor.ts:3901-3902) — a duplicate client-side check cannot constrain an attacker who controls the browser, so the request is defense-in-depth/regression durability, not an exploitable weakness. The shadow-mode webhook (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105, verified real) only matters given an actual client bypass, and none exists; the reviewer concedes as much ("no live bypass today").

verdict.reason: The described ordering is real (imageKeyHandler at text-editor.ts:865 runs before the readOnly guard at text-editor.ts:894, and handleImageMouseDown at editor.ts:2538-2605 does permit image selection in read-only), but every branch reachable inside imageKeyHandler that can mutate the document is independently guarded, so no write is reachable in a read-only mount. Delete/Backspace (editor.ts:2382-2386) calls deleteSelectedImageInline, which returns immediately on `if (readOnly || !selectedImage)` at editor.ts:2283 before docStore.snapshot()/doc.deleteText at 2296-2297. Cmd/Ctrl+X (editor.ts:2371-2373) returns true without preventDefault and defers to the native cut event, where handleCut self-guards at text-editor.ts:1237-1240. Escape (2374-2381) and the arrow branches (2392-2412) only touch cursor/selectedImage/render — view state that read-only already permits via the nav-key allowance at text-editor.ts:895-911. The catch-all (2419-2421) returns false and therefore does reach the enforced readOnly guard at text-editor.ts:894. The newly granted textarea focus (editor.ts:1255-1259) likewise reaches only guarded write paths: handleInput (text-editor.ts:768-771), handleCompositionStart (text-editor.ts:692), insertText (text-editor.ts:639). The finding itself concedes no mutating branch is unguarded today and argues only that future branches would be write-enabled by default; under the Security rubric that is a defense-in-depth/hardening suggestion (minor/nit), not a major weakness — there is no reachable write, no bypass, and no exploit chain.
